analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: a date bump (line 3) and a new prose description near line 1293 of PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup. That text says the lookup snapshots all hits before promoting them between its two bounded generations, so a rotation mid-lookup cannot turn a later piece into a miss. It also says token arrays share storage during the snapshot and that existing admission and byte bounds still apply. No executable code, config, wire contract or security control is modified in the supplied evidence. The supplied units (base lines 2428-2961) are unchanged surrounding text and show no modifications.

Threat-model relevance: the prompt-piece token cache is scoped to the prefix-cache scope (cacheSalt). It touches T-041 only indirectly, because a timing or hit/miss channel could exist if the scope were wrong. The doc states reuse stays within the same prefix-cache scope, which matches the coordinator-authored account scoping in T-041. The doc change does not widen scope, TTL, disk or at-rest surface. The snapshot sharing of token arrays is a copy-on-write value semantics claim, so no cross-scope leakage is implied.

Remaining unverified: the actual Swift implementation of PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup is not supplied. The doc cannot confirm that the snapshot or promotion preserves scope isolation and the byte bounds, or whether it affects timing or memory residency of prompt tokens (A-001). A reviewer of the code change should check that the cache key includes the scope, that promotion cannot cross scopes, and that memory bounds hold with shared array storage. Since this is a docs-only unit, no finding is warranted.
